about: A Zork-like cave adventure. You start in a barrow with a lantern and sword, cross a ravine, and explore caverns and a formal garden. A Wizard pops in and out. Treasures lie south past a stone door and a room that will not keep still.

done.why: I had seen the opening area and hit a polite wall at the unicorn. I did not know how to go further, so I stopped.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, waved his wand and I dropped the lamp. He also told me where the treasures are.
Going south into the dark with no warning about needing light.
Replies like 'That sentence isn't one I recognize' when I typed a longer sentence.
The unicorn description: the ribbon is meant for somebody in particular.

wished: To know what the key and the unicorn were for.
To be told what words the game understands.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid
It will wait for her. You need not.
lines.why: A good line that closed the door politely.

fun.why: Pleasant exploring with some charming moments.

engagement.why: The wizard's hints gave me a direction.

difficulty.why: Mostly fair. The dark tunnel was a surprise, but I had a lamp.

interestingness.why: The newspaper and the wizard hint at a larger story.

prose.why: Evocative descriptions and a witty unicorn.
